question: Is jaws-v1 a better deck? The swap that decides it: Fiery Emancipation (triples all our damage, RRR) out for Jaws, Relentless Predator (Blood on every hit, a ping per Blood or Treasure sacrificed) -- keep it, or go back to the tripler?

contributions.slice: MODE prescribe: Fiery vs Jaws; verbatim (orchestrator notes trimmed). The same agent, on study 006's restated strategy, agreed with cutting Fiery.
contributions.text:
MY PICK: put Fiery Emancipation back and take Jaws out. Keep the rest of jaws-v1 as staged, including the two-drop Humans (Inti, Prince Imrahil) and Mariner.

1. The deck wins with Shabraz's commander damage, and on the branch only one card multiplies it. The cards that change damage are Gratuitous Violence (x2), Torbran, and three double-strike cards (Akroma's Will, Blade Historian, Lizard Blades). Torbran adds nothing to Shabraz: Shabraz is {3}{W}{U}, not red. Fiery was the second multiplier. Jaws adds a red body, not a multiplier. The pilot's own rule (an effect earns its slot only if it multiplies) points at Fiery. Fiery triples Brallin's pings too (stack 007, checker pass).
2. The red premise in the branch's why does not hold up. Red sources went DOWN, from 37 on V14 to 36 on the branch (deck-audit, both lists). The "11 short" went away because the target moved from 48 to 36, not because red was added (the sizing quorum, Q048). With Fiery back the audit will show red short by about 12 again; that comes from the target rule, not worse odds of red on curve than V14 had.
3. Bracket: Fiery is not a Game Changer; the floor stays at 3.
4. Jaws is a five-drop competing with Shabraz for the same turn. No flying, so its Blood depends on combat damage through a ground board (game 009 had two 6/6 dragons). Its best case is real: about 3 per Treasure with Torbran out, and game 009 banked 14 Treasure from Tithe — but that needs Jaws and the pile together, a single game, and Jaws was not in that list.

The log on the current list (008, 009) never saw either card. 008 was a piloting error; 009 a slow, creatureless start and a race — the log argues for keeping the cheap Humans, not for Jaws.

GOLDFISH (one instrument, never the reason; both seen; 10,000 paired games), Fiery back on the branch:
- For Jaws: killed by T6 19.3% -> 21.6%, +2.4 pts [+2.1, +2.7]; damage @T10 +96.3 [+91.7, +100.9]; board power @T6 -0.3; hoard @T10 -0.29 [-0.43, -0.16].
- For Imrahil: killed by T6 +2.0 [+1.7, +2.4], board power -0.6.
- For Inti: killed by T6 +2.1 [+1.7, +2.4], hoard -0.57.
The goldfish says the tripler is worth about 2 points of kill by T6 whatever leaves; it does not pick the cut.

For the pilot: swapping out V14's own multiplier for Jaws is not a clear upgrade. If he wants Jaws kept for the Treasure-ping line, the honest alternative is Fiery in for Prince Imrahil, contested. Trimming red sources should not be part of this swap.

contributions.slice: Fiery vs Jaws argument; verbatim (run list trimmed)
contributions.text:
Lean: keep Jaws. Fiery Emancipation is a high-ceiling, low-median card in this deck, and the branch's recorded losses do not point at it. This is argument, not evidence.

1. The Brallin math is real but needs a precondition. Brallin's pings are damage from a source you control, so stack 007 (checker pass) shows the tripler applies to them: one ping under Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation (stack:007). It also needs Brallin on board, a wheel in hand, and the 6-mana RRR enchantment already resolved. CONTEXT says Brallin is cast late, "his discard ping is no longer the plan. He is a pivot", and that the wheels are the finishers. So the tripler multiplies a plan the pilot has moved off.
2. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density separates the ceiling build ("one spectacular finisher, loses when it's answered") from the median build ("closes from any board"). The tripler is the ceiling pole. It does nothing alone, so it is a "naked all-in" under strategy:critical-mass; three opponents' interaction punishes it.
3. strategy:threat-assessment and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: a 6-mana enchantment that sits there draws attention and spends your deflection budget without a board behind it.
4. Redundancy: the dossier's nearest-by-function neighbour for Fiery Emancipation is Gratuitous Violence at 0.95. Torbran plus Gratuitous Violence already scale the pings; strategy:conversion.payoff-density says payoff density is not the lever.
5. Cost: RRR in a WUR deck is a real tension (the pilot's 2026-11-14 note); Jaws is a single red pip. Q048 records the on-curve red figure as a sizing artifact, so not leaned on.
6. The losses: 008 was a sequencing error ("pilot error, not the list"); 009 a thin keep, no blockers, held Treasure — a tripler does nothing against being attacked on turn 3; the 4 of 9 raced games want cheaper board presence or interaction; game 006 had Fiery Emancipation on board and lost with "no wheel in the digging".
7. Jaws: a 5-mana haste trample body, a threat the turn it lands; Blood is the discard-and-draw loop that feeds Shabraz; it pings when artifacts are sacrificed; Torbran amplifies it. The tripler needs a board; Jaws is the board.

Caveat: the one case where the tripler wins is wheel plus Brallin plus Torbran; no verified count of how often that happens. The goldfish cannot see opposing removal, so it cannot settle this.
open: (1) How often does a wheel line with Brallin on board happen in the pilot's games? (2) Is Jaws's Blood-sacrifice ping reachable on this list, which has few artifact-sacrifice outlets?

Sharknado is a bit of a theme/gaga deck, so I like Jaws for the aesthetic reasons.. but the red source doublers and triplers aren't in our strategy as much anymore ... blood or treasure... just artifacts to sac... wheels to find jaws, maybe a tutor in there to get the big shark
call.reading: Jaws stays on jaws-v1 and Fiery Emancipation stays out: the pilot made Jaws the centre of the deck (artifact tokens sacrificed for pings), and the red multipliers are no longer the plan.
